_: Town building knobs (towns.gd reads them). castle: where a great house's castle may stand when the first, old search (eight headings on the square's ring, all dry) finds no plot: headings around, rings out from the square (0 is the old ring; -1 hugs the square), sizes tried in order, and the share of the plot's edge that may stand over water if the keep's middle is dry.
_sets: castles: pack (the realistic kit's castle and longhall) or kit (castle_builder.gd raises each great house's castle, and house_builder.gd its hall, from the Quaternius kit, sized to the seat's rank: data/assets.json castle.kit); --castles=kit for one run. houses: pack or kit (house_builder.gd's townhouses, cottages and inn in place of the downloaded houses); --houses=kit. Kit roofs and banners take the holder's colour with team colour on (look.json team).
_density: density: how many houses a town raises (towns.gd _real_lots): base + per_size x its size, held between min and max, seat more at a great house's seat; crown: the crown's seat only (art target 01-town, plots shoulder to shoulder behind the square): extra houses, ring_pack (houses' spacing on the rings past the square as a share of their width; 0.95 elsewhere), ring_jitter (the extra gap's most, in units; 0.3 elsewhere), street_gaps (the share of street plots left as a yard or alley; 0.14 elsewhere).
_plots: layout: rings (houses on rings round the square, today's) or plots (town_plots.gd: roads first, burgage plots along them, a fenced yard behind each house; --towns=plots / --towns=rings for one run). plots: set_back (street edge to a house front), yard (a yard's depth behind its house), gap (between two plots' houses), lane_every and lane_length (branch lanes along a road), lanes_per_size and lanes_most (lanes a town lays: (size - 2) x lanes_per_size, at most lanes_most), wander (how much a street bends on level ground), edge_more (how much further the plots run than the old palisade ring), square_ring (houses enclose the square between the roads in; ring_slide: a front turned away by a road in, a landmark or a stall slides on round the edge this far, game units, and is tried again; --ring-slide=off for the old whole-house step; ring_first: the square's ring laid before the trades that stand off the plots, by the castle, the inn and the water, which took the band round the square first in round 4; --ring-first=off as before), fence (the yards' fence: a component in assets.json), yard_things (a yard's working thing in its back corner, each component by its chance: a woodshed, a pen), green (art target town-b: trees between the houses, gardens, hedges; each yard by its chance: tree, a fruit or shade tree at the back of the yard (assets.json town_tree); hedge, a hedge along its side fence (garden_hedge); flowers, a flower bed by the house's back door (garden_flowers); garden, its kitchen garden of vegetable rows (was 0.65); garden_depth, the bed's depth, fewest and most (was 0.3-0.42: with the bed holding a circle as wide as itself it took the whole yard, and batch 6's yards grew 3 trees for 61 houses); tree_ground, the ground a yard tree's trunk keeps others off (its crown overhangs the bed and the fence); square_trees, shade trees round the square's rim before the house fronts (research rule 8: a town centre's trees cluster at its square); edge_trees: trees just outside the town's edge, one per that many units of it), near (a house stands only within this of something already standing, the square, the castle, a landmark or a house, so a town grows out from its heart with one edge and no house alone on the fields; 0 turns it off); crown: the crown's seat's own (art target 01-town: narrow, deep plots shoulder to shoulder along winding streets), and extra, how many more houses it raises on plots. rings: ring streets round the square, each this far out from its edge (game units; art target town-b, Manor Lords: streets circling the market behind its first row), arcs between the castle, the landmarks and the water, lined with houses on both sides; none elsewhere. The crown's seat (round 2 against 01-town: houses loose on grass; now yard 0.4 (was 0.55), gap 0.01 (was 0.02), extra 48 (was 40), so the rows stand back to back; rings [2.6, 4.8] tried in round 3 cut fewer plots, 80 not 92, and stood fewer houses, so back to): rings [2.8, 5.2], edge_more 2.4 (was 1.6), lanes_most 4 (was 14: twelve lanes criss-crossing three roads cut 27 plots and stood 16 houses in batch 6). seat: a great house's seat's own (Goldrock; towns.gd town_rank), town: a market town's (at least min_size), on top of plots as crown's is: every large town rings its square with streets and packs its plots by its size (headless probe, flat land, three roads: a seat 9-14 houses before, 51-57 after; a size 5-6 town 20-23 before, 35-37 after).
_tiers: tiers (town_tiers.gd decides each house): ladder, the house components poorest first (hovel, cottage, townhouse, merchant, burgher, manor: assets.json); corner, the component a corner plot may take (corner_share of the time), a rung up (corner_up). wealth: per zone the weight of each rung, near the square (near) and at the edge (far), eased between: square (the ring facing the square), main (the main streets), lane (the lanes). min_size: the smallest town each rung stands in (a seat counts seat_size bigger); manor_most: manors a town may raise on its plots (0: the manor is a trade, walled with its garden past the edge; trades.list house_manor). No two neighbours on a street are the same model.
_trades: trades (town_trades.gd plans, towns.gd stands them; the land goes to them before the houses): list, in the order they claim land; each stands when the town has one of its needs (the bridge's buildings), or is at least min_size, or (seat) is a great house's seat. where: main (a plot on a main street, t: its window from the square (0) to the edge (1)), lane (a plot on a lane), gate (a main-street plot toward the edge, by the road out), inn (beside the inn on the square, turned along its edge), castle (beside the castle, or the square where there is none), water (on the shore, the nearest dry flat ground to water), high (the highest open ground just past the edge), edge (just past the edge by a main road, toward the fields), downstream (on the shore, the lowest ground past the edge). trade_art: kit (the trades raised from the kit or the catalogue's models) or ai (the image-to-3D models in assets.json ai lists); --trade_art=ai for one run.
_market: centre: the square's centrepiece at its heart in the well's stead, a component (assets.json square_fountain: the Kenney Fantasy Town fountain basin with a brick column and an urn; square_statue: the same with the King on the column, the crown's seat's, art target 01-town), none: the draw well off the heart, as before. market.seat and market.town: a great house's seat's and a market town's square and market (square_r, stalls_more, goods, piles, as the crown's; towns.gd by the town's rank). market.crown: the crown's seat's market at midday (art target 01-town: some twenty at work round the square; town-b: a great paved square full of stalls and goods). square_r: its square's half-width (game units; 1.25 at other seats, was 1.25 here); goods: the heaps at each stall's ends, fewest and most (1-3 elsewhere); piles: heaps of barrels, crates and sacks set down about the square beyond the stalls; stalls_more (stalls past a seat's three, and the Marketplace's two; the kit's stalls are a third as wide as the pack's, so more stand), rows (the stalls in rows facing the square's heart: each row's radius as a share of square_r and its share of the stalls, outer first; one row at 0.8 elsewhere), span (how far either side of the market's middle a row runs, degrees: a row stops when full, so the pack's wide stalls stand fewer), buyers (each stall's buyers, fewest and most; 1-2 elsewhere), smith (a smith at his anvil), carts (carters selling from a cart), porters (porters at the stalls' ends), square_holds (how many villagers the square holds at once with its scene folk; 5 to 10 elsewhere by size), rooms (how many each of its places holds: market, well, tavern, sept), out_most (the most of its people out by day; 40 elsewhere), farmers_to_market (the share of would-be farmers who keep a city trade at the market instead). counter: a stall's counter piled with its wares (comp: the component they come from, assets.json stall_wares: apples, melons, carrots, pots and sacks from the market pack, crates and a barrel of apples from the kit; height and depth out as shares of the stall's width, count low and high, scale of each, span along the counter); well_too: the roofed draw well beside a centrepiece (the crown's statue), well_at its distance from the heart as a share of the square's radius.
_paving: paving (art target town-b: cobbles over the square and the main streets): texture (the kit's stylised stones on earth; the old square-cobbles.jpg read as dirt), tint (a multiply, warm grey-beige), tile (game units one copy of the stone covers), square (the square's paving across, as a multiple of its half-width: 2 reaches its edge, more runs under the house fronts), square_aspect (its depth as a share of its width), streets (the share of each main street, from the square out, laid with setts: crown the crown's seat, seat a great house's seat, town any other), width (a paved street's width as a share of the street's earth).
_lanes: lanes (paved: the ranks whose back lanes are laid in the paving's setts too, with straight-ish kerbs: crown, art target 01-town; research rule 16: dirt lanes 4-5 m with soft edges; the main and ring streets keep their earth and, by rank, their cobbles, paving): the back lanes off the main streets as trodden earth. ground: worn into the land itself where it is Terrain3D's (the square's mud stamped along the lane every `stamp` units, blending into the grass at its edge); otherwise, or with ground false, a decal of `texture` with soft frayed verges and no ruts, tinted `tint`. width: the lane's worn width as a share of a street's (0.34 units, about 2.8 m).
_props: props.sink: how far a prop on the square (stall, wagon, barrels, crates, the well) sits into the ground below the lowest of its middle and four corners (game units; 0.006 is about 5 cm), so nothing hangs over a slope.
_edge: edge (art target town-a/b: the town in its fields): mill_wheat, wheat fields laid round each windmill that stood (how many); orchards, how many orchards by the town's rank (crown, seat, town, village), by the roads out just past the edge; orchard: each one's rows and columns of trees (fewest, most), their spacing (game units; 0.55 is about 4.5 m) and size (a share of assets.json orchard_tree's height).
_farms: farms.fieldRise: the most a farmstead's field's ground may rise across it (game units, about 3 m); steeper and the field is not laid (its paint was cut off in a triangle on a slope).
